title: ITR-4 Deductions: Documents for TY 2026-27 Tax Benefits
description: ITR-4 is filed by individuals, HUFs, and firms opting for the Presumptive Taxation Scheme under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, and 44AE. This scheme simplifies tax fil.

faq.q: Who is eligible to file ITR-4?
faq.a: ITR-4 is for resident individuals, HUFs, and firms (excluding LLPs) whose total income includes business income under Section 44AD or 44AE, or professional income under Section 44ADA, and whose total income does not exceed ₹50 lakhs.

faq.q: Can I claim expenses if I opt for presumptive taxation?
faq.a: No, if you opt for presumptive taxation, you cannot claim any business expenses like rent, salaries, or depreciation. The presumptive income (e.g., 6%, 8%, or 50% of turnover/receipts) is considered your final profit after all expenses.

faq.q: What if my actual income is lower than the presumptive income?
faq.a: If your actual income is lower than the presumptive income and you wish to declare this lower income, you cannot file ITR-4. You would need to maintain proper books of accounts and get them audited under Section 44AB.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to pay advance tax if I file ITR-4?
faq.a: Yes, if your estimated tax liability for the year exceeds ₹10,000, you are required to pay advance tax. For ITR-4 filers under Sections 44AD/44ADA, the entire advance tax must be paid in a single instalment by 15th March of the financial year.

faq.q: Can I claim deductions under Chapter VI-A (like 80C, 80D) even with presumptive income?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. Even after declaring income under the presumptive taxation scheme, you are fully eligible to claim deductions under Chapter VI-A of the Income Tax Act, such as those under Sections 80C, 80D, 80E, 80G, and 80TTA/80TTB, among others.

faq.q: What is the turnover limit for ITR-4 under Section 44AD?
faq.a: The turnover or gross receipts limit for businesses opting for presumptive taxation under Section 44AD is ₹3 crore for Tax Year 2026-27, provided certain conditions are met regarding cash receipts.

faq.q: Do I need to maintain detailed books of accounts for ITR-4?
faq.a: No, one of the main benefits of opting for presumptive taxation and filing ITR-4 is that you are exempt from maintaining detailed books of accounts under Section 44AA. However, it is prudent to keep basic records of your gross receipts and proofs for any deductions claimed.
